intent.raw_query: Safari Kenya family of 3, $8000, 10 days, July 2026

experiences.name: Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari
experiences.description: Witness the world-famous Great Migration where millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles cross the Mara River in one of nature's most spectacular events. Game drives in open 4x4 vehicles offer close encounters with the Big Five including lions, elephants, leopards, buffalos, and rhinos in their natural habitat.
experiences.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Backdrop
experiences.description: Observe some of Africa's largest elephant herds roaming freely against the stunning backdrop of Mount Kilimanjaro. Amboseli is renowned for its large tuskers and offers exceptional photography opportunities. Guided nature walks with Maasai rangers provide deeper insight into the ecosystem and local wildlife tracking techniques.

experiences.name: Ol Pejeta Conservancy Rhino Tracking
experiences.description: Visit the largest black rhino sanctuary in East Africa and home to the last two northern white rhinos on Earth. Guided bush walks and game drives allow intimate encounters with rhinos, chimpanzees, and diverse wildlife. The conservancy blends conservation education with thrilling wildlife experiences in a responsible and sustainable setting.

experiences.name: Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Bird Safari
experiences.description: Explore the alkaline shores of Lake Nakuru, famously painted pink by thousands of flamingos and home to over 400 bird species. The national park also shelters white and black rhinos, Rothschild giraffes, and leopards. A scenic drive around the lake offers breathtaking panoramic views and incredible birdwatching opportunities for nature enthusiasts.
experiences.location: Lake Nakuru National Park, Nakuru County

experiences.name: Maasai Cultural Village & Sundowner Bush Dinner
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in authentic Maasai culture with a guided visit to a traditional manyatta village, learning about warrior traditions, beadwork, and ancient customs. End the day with a magical bush sundowner dinner under the African stars, enjoying traditional Kenyan cuisine including nyama choma, ugali, and sukuma wiki while listening to Maasai songs around a campfire.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Kenya
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - arrival day
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - arrival day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and arrange budget airport transfer (matatu or shared shuttle) to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in and settle into your beachfront accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable - in transit
meals.lunch: Not applicable - in transit
meals.dinner: Grab a light snack or street food near the airport if hungry before transfer (budget ~500 KES / $4)

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange your airport transfer in advance to save money. Avoid unofficial taxis at the airport. Keep small Kenyan shillings handy for tips. Rest well for the adventures ahead!

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely wake-up, take a relaxed morning walk along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort. Explore the coastline, watch local fishermen, and soak in the warm 25°C weather. Visit a nearby local market to exchange currency and pick up snacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local neighborhood on foot or by tuk-tuk (budget ~200 KES). Visit a nearby nature trail or public beach area. Chat with locals to get tips on affordable safari options. Visit a local curio shop to browse handmade Kenyan crafts without pressure to buy.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset view from the beachfront. Head to a local restaurant near the resort for a casual dinner. Relax and plan your upcoming safari days.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort or a nearby local cafe - try mandazi (fried dough) and chai tea (~300 KES / $2.50)
meals.lunch: Street food lunch - nyama choma (grilled meat) or a chapati wrap from a local vendor (~400 KES / $3)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a budget local restaurant near the resort - try ugali with sukuma wiki (collard greens) and fish (~600 KES / $5)

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 is an orientation and recovery day. Stay hydrated in the warm weather. Apply sunscreen as temperatures reach 25°C. Start researching shared safari van options for upcoming days to save significantly on costs.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning departure (6:00 AM) via shared budget safari van toward Tsavo East National Park - one of Kenya's largest and most affordable national parks. Enjoy the scenic drive through the Kenyan countryside. Arrive at the park gate and begin your game drive looking for elephants, lions, and buffalo.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the afternoon game drive through Tsavo East. Look for the famous red elephants of Tsavo, hippos at Galana River, and diverse birdlife. Enjoy a packed lunch at a designated picnic area inside the park with stunning bush views.
day_by_day.evening: Return drive back to Aegean Bliss Resort. Arrive by early evening, freshen up, and relax. Share safari stories with fellow travelers at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort before departure - bread, fruit, and tea (~250 KES / $2)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch prepared in advance or purchased at park entrance - sandwiches, fruit, and water (~500 KES / $4)
meals.dinner: Budget dinner at a local eatery near the resort - beans stew with ugali and a soda (~700 KES / $6)

day_by_day.notes: Book a shared safari van in advance to split costs among travelers - budget approximately 3,000-5,000 KES ($25-$40) per person including park entry fees on a group deal. Bring binoculars, a hat, and sunscreen. July is excellent for wildlife viewing as vegetation is lower in the dry season.

day_by_day.morning: Take a guided nature walk along the coastal forest or mangrove area near the resort. Explore the rich birdlife and coastal ecosystems. A local guide can be hired affordably (~1,000 KES / $8) for a 2-hour walk. Look for kingfishers, herons, and coastal birds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local Maasai or Mijikenda cultural village near the coast for an authentic and educational experience. Learn about traditional customs, dances, and crafts. Many villages offer affordable entry (~500 KES / $4). Browse locally made beadwork and baskets.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Enjoy a beach sunset walk. Visit a local beach bar or restaurant for an affordable dinner with an ocean view.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the resort or a local cafe - eggs, bread, fruit, and chai (~400 KES / $3)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a local village or roadside cafe - samosas, mandazi, and fresh juice (~350 KES / $3)
meals.dinner: Seafood dinner at a budget beachside restaurant - grilled tilapia or prawns with rice (~800 KES / $7)

day_by_day.notes: Respect cultural norms when visiting local villages - ask permission before taking photographs. Negotiate cultural village entry fees politely. The coastal forests are rich in biodiversity and worth exploring slowly. Carry insect repellent for the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day trip to Shimba Hills National Reserve - a coastal rainforest reserve home to the rare sable antelope, elephants, leopards, and over 200 bird species. Depart early by shared transport or matatu (~500 KES). Morning game drive or guided forest walk through the lush green hills.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Shimba Hills. Visit the Sheldrick Falls waterfall inside the reserve - a beautiful natural highlight. Enjoy a picnic lunch surrounded by forest sounds and wildlife. Look for colobus monkeys in the treetops.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by late afternoon. Relax on the beach as the sun sets. Enjoy a quiet evening with dinner at a local budget restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before departure - porridge or bread with peanut butter and tea (~250 KES / $2)
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch packed from a local market - fruits, bread, boiled eggs, and water (~400 KES / $3.50)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local restaurant - chicken stew with rice and vegetables (~650 KES / $5.50)

day_by_day.notes: Shimba Hills entry fee is approximately 1,050 KES ($9) for non-residents - very affordable compared to other reserves. Hire a Kenya Wildlife Service ranger guide for safety and enhanced wildlife spotting (~500 KES tip recommended). The forest is cooler than the coast - bring a light layer.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling or glass-bottom boat trip at a nearby marine park or coral reef (budget option: group glass-bottom boat ~1,500 KES / $12 per person). Explore colorful coral gardens and tropical fish in the warm Indian Ocean waters. Perfect for wildlife lovers extending their nature experience underwater.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local snake park or reptile sanctuary in the area for an educational wildlife experience (~500 KES entry). Learn about Kenya's diverse reptile species including pythons, chameleons, and tortoises. Great for wildlife enthusiasts on a budget.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through a local night market or food street near the resort. Sample various Kenyan street foods and fresh tropical fruits. Enjoy the vibrant local atmosphere and interact with vendors.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort - fresh tropical fruit platter, bread, and coffee (~350 KES / $3)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a beachside budget cafe - fish and chips or rice with beans (~600 KES / $5)
meals.dinner: Street food dinner at the night market - mix of samosas, roasted corn, grilled meats, and fresh juice (~500 KES / $4)

day_by_day.notes: Check tide times before the boat trip for the best snorkeling visibility. Bring a waterproof bag for your valuables. The marine park is a fantastic wildlife experience that complements your land safari days. Haggling is acceptable and expected at night markets - do so respectfully.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day budget safari excursion to Tsavo West National Park. Depart by 6:00 AM via shared safari van. Morning game drive to spot lions, cheetahs, zebras, giraffes, and the famous Mzima Springs where hippos and crocodiles live in crystal-clear water fed by underground volcanic springs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Shetani Lava Flow - a dramatic black lava landscape within Tsavo West. Continue the afternoon game drive looking for rhinos at the Ngulia Rhino Sanctuary. Enjoy a packed lunch at a designated rest area with panoramic views of the Chyulu Hills.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the return journey to the resort. Arrive by 7:00-8:00 PM. Enjoy a well-deserved dinner and rest after a full day of wildlife adventure.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before departure - energy bars, banana, and tea (~200 KES / $1.50)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch - sandwiches, fruits, biscuits, and water (~500 KES / $4)
meals.dinner: Hearty dinner at the resort restaurant or nearby local eatery - beef stew with ugali and greens (~750 KES / $6)

day_by_day.notes: Tsavo West and Tsavo East are often combined in budget tours. Booking both as a 2-day package can reduce costs further. Mzima Springs is a highlight - the underground viewing chamber lets you watch hippos underwater for free with park entry. Bring a charged camera with a zoom lens.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning at the resort. Take a sunrise beach walk and enjoy the peaceful coastal atmosphere. Visit a nearby local market to shop for affordable Kenyan souvenirs - kikoi fabrics, wooden carvings, and beaded jewelry. Practice your bargaining skills for the best deals.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local botanical garden or nature reserve near the coast for a peaceful afternoon of birdwatching and nature photography. Bring a notebook to document the bird species spotted throughout your trip. Alternatively, take a budget cycling tour of the local coastal villages (~1,000 KES / $8 bike rental).
day_by_day.evening: Attend a local cultural performance or beach bonfire event if available near the resort. Enjoy traditional Kenyan music and dance. Relax with a cold Tusker beer or fresh coconut water on the beach.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local cafe - mkate wa ufuta (sesame bread) with eggs and chai (~300 KES / $2.50)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local market food stall - pilau rice with kachumbari salad (~450 KES / $3.50)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a beachside budget restaurant - coconut fish curry with rice (~800 KES / $7)

day_by_day.notes: This is a lighter day to recharge before the final safari push. Use the morning market visit to buy gifts and souvenirs - prices are significantly lower at local markets than tourist shops. Fresh coconut water from roadside vendors is both refreshing and very affordable (~100 KES).

day_by_day.morning: Early morning birdwatching excursion at a local wetland, estuary, or mangrove forest near the resort. Kenya is a world-class birdwatching destination with over 1,100 species. Hire a local birding guide (~1,500 KES / $12) for a 3-hour guided walk to spot flamingos, kingfishers, fish eagles, and sunbirds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local conservation project or wildlife rescue center in the area. Many centers welcome visitors for small donations and offer educational tours about Kenya's conservation efforts. Learn about anti-poaching initiatives and community conservation programs.
day_by_day.evening: Final special dinner at a slightly upgraded local restaurant to celebrate your Kenyan adventure. Try a full traditional Kenyan meal spread. Reflect on your trip highlights and pack for departure.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast - boiled eggs, bread, and strong Kenyan coffee (~300 KES / $2.50)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a local cafe after the morning walk - githeri (corn and beans) with a soda (~400 KES / $3)
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at a mid-range local restaurant - full Kenyan spread with nyama choma, ugali, sukuma wiki, and kachumbari (~1,200 KES / $10)

day_by_day.notes: July is an excellent month for birdwatching in coastal Kenya as migratory birds are present. Download a Kenya bird identification app before your trip (free options available). The conservation center visit is a meaningful way to support local wildlife efforts and learn about Kenya's ecological challenges.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at Aegean Bliss Resort. Wake up early for one last sunrise beach walk and a swim in the Indian Ocean. Pack your bags and check out of the resort. Store luggage at the front desk if your flight is later in the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, take a final tuk-tuk ride through the local area for last-minute souvenir shopping or a final meal at a favorite local spot. Head to the airport via shared shuttle or budget transfer (~500-800 KES). Arrive at the airport at least 3 hours before international departure.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Kenya with incredible memories of wildlife, nature, and cultural experiences. Reflect on the amazing budget safari adventure completed across Tsavo East, Tsavo West, Shimba Hills, and the beautiful Kenyan coast.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at the resort or a nearby cafe - enjoy a full Kenyan breakfast one last time (~400 KES / $3)
meals.lunch: Quick lunch near the resort or airport - chapati with lentil soup or a packed snack for the journey (~400 KES / $3)
meals.dinner: Airport meal or in-flight meal depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your return flight details the night before. Keep some Kenyan shillings for airport tips and last-minute purchases. Declare any wildlife products (like certain wooden items) at customs if required. Budget summary for the 10-day trip: accommodation at Aegean Bliss, safari park entries (~15,000 KES total), meals (~500-800 KES/day average), and local transport (~3,000 KES total) keeps the trip well within a budget-conscious range of approximately $300-$400 USD excluding flights.

trip_options.title: Classic Kenya Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage, and meet your pre-arranged airport transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort in the Beachfront area. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your room.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane
meals.dinner: Light late-night snack or room service at Aegean Bliss Resort upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book your airport transfer in advance to avoid delays at night. Keep essential items in your carry-on for easy access after a long flight. The resort's 24-hour front desk will accommodate your late check-in. Exchange some currency or use the ATM at the airport for local Kenyan Shillings (KES).

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take a relaxed orientation walk along the beachfront to acclimatize to Kenya's warm summer weather (25°C highs). Explore the resort grounds and nearby coastal area to get your bearings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby local market or coastal town to pick up essentials, browse Kenyan crafts, and soak in the local atmosphere. Enjoy the warm Indian Ocean breeze and perhaps dip your toes in the water along the beachfront.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sundowner drink on the resort terrace watching the coastal sunset. Have a relaxed dinner at the resort restaurant to recover from jet lag before the adventure-packed days ahead.

meals.breakfast: Full buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort – included or mid-range resort pricing (~$15–20 USD)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a local coastal café – try Swahili dishes like pilau rice or grilled fish (~$8–12 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort restaurant – fresh seafood and Kenyan staples (~$20–30 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 is intentionally relaxed to allow recovery from jet lag before multi-day safari trips begin. Stay hydrated and apply sunscreen – the equatorial sun is strong even at 25°C. Confirm all upcoming safari bookings and transfers with the resort concierge today.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning departure by road or domestic flight to the Maasai Mara National Reserve – one of Africa's greatest wildlife destinations. Arrive at your mid-range tented camp or lodge in the Mara in time for a briefing with your guide. Begin your first game drive across the vast savannah grasslands.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon game drive in the Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari – witness the world-famous Great Migration where millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles traverse the Mara ecosystem. July is peak migration season, making this an extraordinary spectacle. Look out for predators like lions, cheetahs, and leopards hunting along the migration routes.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the tented camp as the sun sets over the Mara plains. Enjoy a bush-style dinner under the stars with fellow travelers and your guide sharing stories of the day's sightings.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at resort before departure or packed breakfast en route
meals.lunch: Bush lunch provided by the safari camp or packed picnic lunch in the Mara (~included in safari package)
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Maasai Mara tented camp – traditional Kenyan and continental dishes (~included or $25–35 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Book a reputable mid-range safari camp in the Maasai Mara in advance – options like Mara Serena Safari Lodge or Fig Tree Camp offer good value. Pack light layers as mornings on the savannah can be cool (~15°C) before warming up. Bring binoculars, a camera with zoom lens, and insect repellent. The drive from Nairobi to Mara is approximately 5–6 hours or 45 minutes by domestic flight from Wilson Airport.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up for a spectacular sunrise game drive in the Maasai Mara. This is the best time to spot big cats on the move and witness the golden light over the savannah. Keep eyes peeled for river crossings – July is prime wildebeest crossing season at the Mara River.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a traditional Maasai Cultural Village – immerse yourself in authentic Maasai culture with a guided visit to a traditional manyatta village. Learn about warrior traditions, beadwork, and the Maasai's coexistence with wildlife. Purchase handmade crafts directly from community artisans to support local livelihoods.
day_by_day.evening: Maasai Sundowner Bush Dinner – enjoy a magical evening with sundowner cocktails on a scenic kopje (rocky outcrop) overlooking the plains, followed by a traditional bush dinner set up under the African sky. Listen to Maasai songs and stories around the campfire.

meals.breakfast: Early morning packed coffee and snacks before the sunrise drive; full breakfast back at camp
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Maasai cultural village or camp (~included in tour or $10–15 USD)
meals.dinner: Sundowner Bush Dinner – included in the Maasai Cultural Village & Sundowner experience package (~$60–80 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Maasai Cultural Village visit typically costs $20–40 USD per person and includes a guided tour and cultural performance. Respect cultural norms – ask permission before photographing community members. The sundowner experience is best booked through your safari camp or a local operator the day before.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning game drive in the Maasai Mara with your guide. Focus on any wildlife you may have missed – elephants, hippos at the river, or elusive leopards in the fig trees. Depart the Mara after breakfast and travel toward Lake Nakuru (approximately 3–4 hours by road via Narok).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Lake Nakuru National Park. Begin the Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Bird Safari – explore the alkaline shores famously painted pink by thousands of flamingos. The lake is also home to white and black rhinos, Rothschild giraffes, lions, and over 400 bird species. Afternoon game drive around the lake's perimeter.
day_by_day.evening: Check into a mid-range lodge near Lake Nakuru such as Sarova Lion Hill Game Lodge or Lake Nakuru Lodge. Enjoy dinner at the lodge with views of the surrounding forest and escarpment.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Maasai Mara camp before departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch en route or stop at a local eatery in Narok town (~$8–12 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Lake Nakuru Lodge – buffet-style Kenyan and continental cuisine (~$20–30 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Lake Nakuru National Park entrance fees are approximately $60 USD per person per day. The flamingo numbers vary seasonally but July typically sees good populations. The park is also a rhino sanctuary, so keep cameras ready. The drive from Maasai Mara to Lake Nakuru passes through beautiful Rift Valley escarpment scenery – a highlight in itself.

day_by_day.morning: Full morning dedicated to the Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Bird Safari. Take a guided walking trail (where permitted) along the lakeshore for close-up flamingo and pelican photography. Spot Rothschild giraffes, waterbuck, and baboons in the yellow fever acacia woodlands.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Ol Pejeta Conservancy (approximately 2.5–3 hours north via Nakuru town). Arrive and check into a mid-range accommodation such as Sweetwaters Serena Camp or Ol Pejeta Bush Camp. Take an introductory afternoon game drive through the conservancy's open plains.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the camp and enjoy a briefing about tomorrow's rhino tracking experience. Dinner at the camp with fellow conservancy guests.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Lake Nakuru Lodge
meals.lunch: Lunch at a restaurant in Nakuru town en route – try a local Kenyan buffet (nyama choma, ugali, sukuma wiki) (~$6–10 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ol Pejeta camp – included in accommodation package or ~$25–35 USD

day_by_day.notes: Ol Pejeta Conservancy is located near Nanyuki at the foot of Mount Kenya. The journey passes through the scenic Laikipia Plateau. Book your conservancy accommodation well in advance as it is a popular destination. Ol Pejeta is also home to chimpanzees in a sanctuary – a unique bonus in a savannah setting.

day_by_day.morning: Ol Pejeta Conservancy Rhino Tracking – join a guided rhino tracking experience to visit the largest black rhino sanctuary in East Africa. Meet the conservancy's dedicated rangers and learn about anti-poaching efforts. You will also have the rare and emotional opportunity to see the last two northern white rhinos in the world – Najin and Fatu – under 24-hour armed guard.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon game drive across Ol Pejeta's vast plains. The conservancy hosts the Big Five – lions, leopards, elephants, buffalo, and rhinos. Visit the chimpanzee sanctuary for an optional guided tour (additional fee ~$30 USD). Enjoy sundowner drinks on the plains as the sun dips behind Mount Kenya.
day_by_day.evening: Campfire dinner at Ol Pejeta under a spectacular equatorial sky. The conservancy's low light pollution makes for outstanding stargazing – ask your guide to point out the Southern Cross and other constellations.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the camp before the rhino tracking departure
meals.lunch: Bush picnic lunch provided by the conservancy or back at camp (~included)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ol Pejeta camp – campfire-style with Kenyan and continental options (~included or $25–30 USD)

day_by_day.notes: The northern white rhino visit is one of the most profound wildlife experiences on Earth and not to be missed. Rhino tracking fees are typically included in the conservancy entrance fee (~$90 USD per person per day). Wear neutral-colored clothing (khaki, olive, beige) for all game drives. Keep voices low and movements calm around wildlife.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Ol Pejeta Conservancy after breakfast and travel south to Amboseli National Park (approximately 5–6 hours via Nairobi or by domestic flight). If driving, enjoy the changing landscapes from the Laikipia Plateau through Nairobi and into the Amboseli basin. Arrive at your mid-range lodge such as Kibo Safari Camp or Ol Tukai Lodge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Backdrop – begin your first Amboseli game drive. Amboseli is famous for its massive elephant herds – some of Africa's largest and most studied. Watch these gentle giants roam freely across the dusty plains with the iconic snow-capped peak of Mount Kilimanjaro (5,895m) rising dramatically on the horizon.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner at an elevated viewpoint or the lodge's terrace with Kilimanjaro views at golden hour – one of Africa's most iconic photographic moments. Dinner at the lodge.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Ol Pejeta before departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch en route or lunch at a Nairobi restaurant if passing through (~$10–15 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Amboseli lodge – Kenyan and international cuisine with views (~$25–35 USD)

day_by_day.notes: July mornings typically offer the clearest views of Kilimanjaro before afternoon clouds build up – plan your game drives accordingly. Amboseli National Park entrance is approximately $60 USD per person per day. Consider a domestic flight from Nanyuki to Amboseli to save travel time (approximately 1 hour, ~$150–200 USD one way).

day_by_day.morning: Early sunrise game drive in Amboseli National Park for the best Kilimanjaro visibility and elephant activity. The Amboseli elephant families are habituated to vehicles, allowing for incredibly close and intimate wildlife encounters. Watch calves play in the swamps while bulls spar in the background.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Amboseli swamp area – a lush oasis in the otherwise dusty basin fed by underground streams from Kilimanjaro's glaciers. Hippos, buffalo, and hundreds of bird species congregate here. Afternoon game drive focusing on predators – lions and cheetahs hunt on the open plains in the afternoon light.
day_by_day.evening: Final safari evening in Amboseli. Enjoy a special farewell bush dinner or a special dinner at the lodge celebrating the incredible wildlife experiences of the past week. Reflect on the journey with fellow travelers over a glass of Kenyan wine or Tusker beer.

meals.breakfast: Early light snack before sunrise drive; full breakfast back at lodge
meals.lunch: Lunch at the lodge or a bush picnic lunch in the park (~included or $12–18 USD)
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner at Amboseli lodge – order à la carte for a treat (~$30–45 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Amboseli is dusty – bring a buff or bandana to cover your face during game drives. Sunscreen and sunglasses are essential. The swamp area is best visited in the afternoon when animals congregate to drink and feed. Photography tip: position your vehicle with Kilimanjaro behind the elephants for the iconic shot – early morning light is best.

day_by_day.morning: Final optional sunrise game drive in Amboseli (if time permits before departure). Return to the lodge for breakfast and pack up. Depart Amboseli and transfer back to Nairobi (approximately 4 hours by road) or take a short domestic flight. Return to Aegean Bliss Resort for a final night or head directly to Jomo Kenyatta International Airport depending on your outbound flight schedule.
day_by_day.afternoon: If time allows before your flight, explore Nairobi's highlights – visit the Giraffe Centre (feed endangered Rothschild giraffes, ~$15 USD), the David Sheldrick Wildlife Trust elephant orphanage (free, donations welcome, morning only – book ahead), or browse the Kazuri Beads workshop and Utamaduni Craft Centre for last-minute souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Nairobi at a celebrated mid-range restaurant such as Carnivore Restaurant (iconic Kenyan game meat experience) or The Talisman in Karen for upscale Kenyan cuisine. Transfer to the airport for your departure flight.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Amboseli lodge before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch in Nairobi – try a local restaurant in Karen or Westlands (~$12–20 USD)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Carnivore Restaurant or The Talisman, Nairobi (~$30–50 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your international departure for check-in and security at JKIA. Keep some Kenyan Shillings for last-minute purchases and tips. It is customary to tip safari guides ($10–20 USD per day) and camp staff ($5–10 USD per day) – prepare tip envelopes before your final day. Ensure all wildlife souvenirs purchased comply with CITES regulations – avoid ivory, shells, or animal products.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Kenya Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari
experiences.description: Witness the world-famous Great Migration where millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles cross the Mara River in one of nature's most spectacular events. Game drives in open 4x4 vehicles offer close encounters with the Big Five including lions, elephants, leopards, buffalos, and rhinos in their natural habitat.
experiences.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Backdrop
experiences.description: Observe some of Africa's largest elephant herds roaming freely against the stunning backdrop of Mount Kilimanjaro. Amboseli is renowned for its large tuskers and offers exceptional photography opportunities. Guided nature walks with Maasai rangers provide deeper insight into the ecosystem and local wildlife tracking techniques.

experiences.name: Ol Pejeta Conservancy Rhino Tracking
experiences.description: Visit the largest black rhino sanctuary in East Africa and home to the last two northern white rhinos on Earth. Guided bush walks and game drives allow intimate encounters with rhinos, chimpanzees, and diverse wildlife. The conservancy blends conservation education with thrilling wildlife experiences in a responsible and sustainable setting.

experiences.name: Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Bird Safari
experiences.description: Explore the alkaline shores of Lake Nakuru, famously painted pink by thousands of flamingos and home to over 400 bird species. The national park also shelters white and black rhinos, Rothschild giraffes, and leopards. A scenic drive around the lake offers breathtaking panoramic views and incredible birdwatching opportunities for nature enthusiasts.
experiences.location: Lake Nakuru National Park, Nakuru County

experiences.name: Maasai Cultural Village & Sundowner Bush Dinner
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in authentic Maasai culture with a guided visit to a traditional manyatta village, learning about warrior traditions, beadwork, and ancient customs. End the day with a magical bush sundowner dinner under the African stars, enjoying traditional Kenyan cuisine including nyama choma, ugali, and sukuma wiki while listening to Maasai songs around a campfire.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Nairobi Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Meet your dedicated luxury concierge and private transfer driver. Enjoy a smooth, air-conditioned private vehicle transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, receive a welcome drink and a brief resort orientation from the night manager.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight or airport lounge dining
meals.lunch: Not applicable — in-flight or airport lounge dining
meals.dinner: Light late-night welcome platter and beverages arranged by the resort upon arrival — charcuterie, local cheeses, tropical fruits, and Kenyan herbal teas

day_by_day.notes: Given the 22:30 arrival, all Day 1 activity is limited to arrival logistics and settling in. Ensure all luggage is confirmed with the porter. Request a late breakfast arrangement for Day 2 morning. Resort concierge will brief you on the full itinerary the following morning.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely late breakfast at the resort. Take a guided orientation walk of the Aegean Bliss Resort grounds, beachfront, and amenities with your personal concierge. Relax by the infinity pool overlooking the Indian Ocean and begin acclimatizing to the Kenyan coastal warmth.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy a private beachfront wellness session — choose from a traditional Swahili massage, hot stone therapy, or aromatherapy at the resort's luxury spa. Afterwards, take a short guided nature walk along the coastline to spot local shore birds and coastal flora unique to Kenya's beachfront ecosystem.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails on the private beach terrace watching the Indian Ocean sunset. Enjoy a welcome dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant featuring a curated menu of Swahili-fusion cuisine with fresh locally caught seafood.

meals.breakfast: Lavish buffet breakfast at the resort's ocean-view restaurant — fresh tropical fruits, Kenyan chai, eggs cooked to order, freshly baked pastries, and smoked fish
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch — grilled prawns, avocado salad, fresh coconut water, and artisanal flatbreads at the resort's beach club
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort's signature restaurant — five-course Swahili-fusion tasting menu featuring lobster bisque, grilled barracuda, coconut pilau rice, and passion fruit panna cotta paired with curated East African wines

day_by_day.notes: This is a recovery and orientation day after the late arrival. Keep the pace relaxed. Confirm all upcoming safari logistics and internal flights with the concierge today. Ensure safari gear (neutral-colored clothing, binoculars, sunscreen) is ready for Day 3 departure.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning private charter flight from the coastal airstrip to Amboseli National Park. Upon landing, meet your expert Amboseli guide and transfer to your luxury tented camp. Begin the Amboseli Elephant Watching experience — game drive through the park's open plains to observe Africa's largest elephant herds roaming freely against the iconic snow-capped backdrop of Mount Kilimanjaro at its most photogenic morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the afternoon game drive deeper into Amboseli's swamp areas, known for extraordinary elephant activity, hippos, and a rich variety of birdlife. Your private guide will share in-depth knowledge of elephant family dynamics and conservation efforts. Visit the Observation Hill for panoramic views of the entire ecosystem.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the luxury tented camp for sundowner drinks on your private veranda as the Kilimanjaro silhouette glows at dusk. Enjoy a candlelit bush dinner under the stars with fellow guests or privately in your tent.

meals.breakfast: Early pre-departure breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — energy-rich continental spread with Kenyan coffee, fresh juices, and pastries
meals.lunch: Bush picnic lunch served in the field by your guide — gourmet sandwiches, grilled chicken, seasonal salads, chilled lemonade, and fresh fruit
meals.dinner: Three-course candlelit dinner at the luxury tented camp — roasted lamb shank with Kenyan spices, sautéed wild mushrooms, and a decadent chocolate fondant with local honey

day_by_day.notes: July is an excellent time for Amboseli — dry season means sparse vegetation and outstanding wildlife visibility. Mount Kilimanjaro is often clearest in the early morning, so the sunrise game drive is essential. Bring a light jacket for the early morning charter flight. Camera with a telephoto lens is highly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Dawn game drive in Amboseli departing at 06:00 — the golden hour light is perfect for photography as elephant herds move from the swamps to the open plains. Look for lions, cheetahs, and large buffalo herds that are frequently spotted at this hour. Return to camp for a full breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local Maasai community near Amboseli for a brief cultural introduction — interact with Maasai warriors, learn about their traditional lifestyle, cattle-herding practices, and beadwork craft. This is a premium, respectful, and ethically managed experience arranged by the camp. Return to camp for an afternoon siesta.
day_by_day.evening: Private sundowner drive to a scenic viewpoint with your guide. Enjoy chilled champagne and canapés as the sun sets over Kilimanjaro. Return for a gourmet dinner at the camp's open-air dining area featuring live acoustic Kenyan music.

meals.breakfast: Full English and African fusion breakfast at camp — eggs Benedict, grilled sausages, fresh papaya, Kenyan porridge (uji), and freshly brewed Kenyan single-origin coffee
meals.lunch: Leisurely three-course lunch at the camp's shaded dining pavilion — tomato and coriander soup, grilled tilapia with coconut sauce, and mango sorbet
meals.dinner: Gourmet bush dinner under the stars — slow-braised Kenyan beef short rib, roasted root vegetables, ugali cake, and a vanilla crème brûlée with Kenyan vanilla pods

day_by_day.notes: Full day in Amboseli allows for deep immersion in the ecosystem. The afternoon Maasai visit should be pre-confirmed with the camp. Keep noise low during dawn drives to maximize wildlife sightings. Stay hydrated — temperatures can reach 25°C in the afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Private charter flight from Amboseli to Lake Nakuru National Park. Check in to your luxury lodge overlooking the lake. Begin the Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Bird Safari — explore the alkaline shores painted pink by thousands of lesser and greater flamingos. Your expert birding guide will help identify over 400 recorded bird species in the park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Lake Nakuru safari focusing on the park's remarkable big game — white and black rhinos, lions, leopards, and large herds of buffalo. Lake Nakuru is one of Kenya's best parks for rhino sightings. Visit the Baboon Cliff viewpoint for a sweeping aerial perspective of the entire lake and flamingo formations.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a private sundowner experience at the lodge's elevated terrace with panoramic lake views. Flamingo flocks create a spectacular pink hue at dusk. Dinner at the lodge's fine-dining restaurant featuring a curated menu of Rift Valley-inspired cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Amboseli camp before departure — fresh fruit platter, yogurt, granola, and Kenyan tea
meals.lunch: Welcome lunch at Lake Nakuru luxury lodge — grilled vegetable bruschetta, pan-seared trout from Rift Valley lakes, and a light passion fruit mousse
meals.dinner: Four-course dinner at the lodge — Rift Valley lamb tagine, saffron-scented couscous, roasted seasonal vegetables, and a dark chocolate and cardamom tart paired with South African Pinotage

day_by_day.notes: July is an excellent month for flamingo sightings at Lake Nakuru as water levels are typically favorable. The park is also a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Bring insect repellent for the lakeside evening. Binoculars are essential for birding. The lodge should arrange a packed sundowner basket in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning game drive in Lake Nakuru National Park focusing on the southern woodland areas where leopards are frequently spotted resting in fever trees. Your guide will navigate the park's diverse habitats — from acacia woodland to open grassland — offering a rich variety of predator and prey sightings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Ol Pejeta Conservancy via a scenic private road transfer (approximately 2.5 hours) — check in to your exclusive luxury tented camp inside the conservancy. Begin the Ol Pejeta Rhino Tracking experience: track the last two northern white rhinos on Earth — Najin and Fatu — accompanied by their armed rangers. An incredibly rare and moving wildlife encounter.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive guided walk to the rhino boma at dusk for a final close-up viewing. Return to camp for a premium bush dinner with the conservancy's conservation team sharing insights into northern white rhino preservation efforts.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Lake Nakuru lodge before departure — smoked salmon bagels, poached eggs, tropical fruit, and freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch en route to Ol Pejeta — artisan wraps, chilled gazpacho, cheese board, and sparkling water served in a scenic roadside spot
meals.dinner: Conservation dinner at Ol Pejeta tented camp — fire-grilled Kenyan beef tenderloin, wild herb chimichurri, roasted sweet potatoes, and a passion fruit cheesecake with macadamia crust

day_by_day.notes: The northern white rhino encounter at Ol Pejeta is one of the most exclusive wildlife experiences on Earth — only two individuals remain. Maintain respectful distance and follow ranger instructions at all times. Photography is permitted but flash is strictly prohibited. The transfer from Lake Nakuru to Ol Pejeta is best done with a private vehicle for flexibility.

day_by_day.morning: Dawn game drive inside Ol Pejeta Conservancy — home to the highest density of black rhinos in East Africa, as well as lions, elephants, cheetahs, and a remarkable variety of plains game. Your expert guide will track animals by fresh spoor and radio communication with other rangers for optimal sightings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Sweetwaters Chimpanzee Sanctuary — a unique feature of Ol Pejeta that offers a remarkable primate encounter. Observe rescued chimpanzees in their spacious natural enclosures. Afterwards, enjoy a leisurely afternoon at the camp's swimming pool with views of the Aberdare mountain range.
day_by_day.evening: Private bush sundowner on the conservancy's open plains — your butler sets up a bespoke drinks station with Kenyan craft gin cocktails, local beers, and premium canapés as the African sky turns amber. Return for a stargazing session with the camp's resident astronomer followed by dinner.

meals.breakfast: Bush breakfast served in the field during the morning game drive — fresh coffee, pastries, boiled eggs, and tropical fruits laid out on a safari table in the wilderness
meals.lunch: Lunch at the camp's shaded terrace — grilled chicken skewers with Kenyan pilipili sauce, quinoa salad, and chilled hibiscus juice
meals.dinner: Romantic candlelit dinner for two in a private boma — slow-cooked goat curry with chapati, cucumber raita, roasted plantains, and a Kenyan honey cake with vanilla ice cream

day_by_day.notes: Ol Pejeta is a non-profit conservancy — your visit directly contributes to rhino and wildlife conservation. The chimpanzee sanctuary visit requires a small additional fee that supports sanctuary operations. Evening temperatures can drop to around 15°C at Ol Pejeta's altitude — bring a warm layer. Stargazing is exceptional in July due to clear skies.

day_by_day.morning: Private charter flight from Ol Pejeta/Nanyuki airstrip to the Maasai Mara National Reserve — the pinnacle of the Kenyan safari experience. Check in to your ultra-luxury tented camp. Begin the Great Migration Safari immediately with an afternoon game drive — July is peak Great Migration season with millions of wildebeest, zebras, and Thomson's gazelles flooding the Mara ecosystem.
day_by_day.afternoon: Game drive along the Mara River to witness the dramatic and heart-stopping wildebeest river crossings — one of nature's greatest spectacles. Massive crocodiles and hippos await as the herds plunge into the crocodile-infested waters. Your expert guide will position the vehicle for the best unobstructed views and photographic angles.
day_by_day.evening: Return to camp for a private sundowner on your tent's veranda as the Mara plains glow at golden hour. Attend a camp briefing on the following day's hot air balloon safari. Enjoy a lavish dinner at the camp's central dining area.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Ol Pejeta camp before departure — full hot breakfast with eggs, bacon, grilled tomatoes, and Kenyan coffee
meals.lunch: Welcome lunch at the Maasai Mara luxury camp — Mara-style mezze spread with grilled meats, fresh salads, hummus, and freshly baked flatbreads
meals.dinner: Six-course tasting dinner at the camp's signature dining tent — wild mushroom velouté, Mara-spiced guinea fowl, truffle-infused potato gratin, artisan cheese selection, and a dark chocolate and Kenyan coffee mousse with petit fours

day_by_day.notes: July is the absolute peak season for the Great Migration river crossings in the Maasai Mara. River crossings are unpredictable — patience at the Mara River is key. Your guide will have radio contact with other guides to alert you when crossings are imminent. Book the hot air balloon for Day 9 well in advance as spots fill up quickly during peak season.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up for the premium hot air balloon safari over the Maasai Mara — drift silently above the golden savannah as the sun rises, watching the Great Migration herds move across the plains from a bird's-eye perspective. Spot lions, elephants, and giraffes from above in complete silence. Land in the bush for a traditional champagne breakfast served on white linen tables in the wilderness.
day_by_day.afternoon: Full afternoon game drive focusing on predator activity — July is exceptional for big cat sightings as lions, cheetahs, and leopards follow the migration herds. Visit the Mara Triangle for some of the highest game density in Africa. Your guide will share expert knowledge on big cat behavior and tracking techniques.
day_by_day.evening: Maasai Cultural Village & Sundowner Bush Dinner experience — transfer to an authentic Maasai manyatta village for a guided cultural immersion. Meet Maasai elders and warriors, witness traditional jumping dances (adumu), learn about beadwork and herbal medicine. As the sun sets, a bespoke bush dinner is set up on the open plains with lanterns, fine linen, and a private chef.

meals.breakfast: Champagne bush breakfast after the hot air balloon landing — smoked salmon, eggs Benedict, fresh fruit platters, pastries, and premium sparkling wine served on the open plains
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch in the Mara Triangle — cold-cut charcuterie board, grilled vegetable tarts, artisan bread, and chilled sparkling water
meals.dinner: Exclusive Maasai bush dinner on the open plains — wood-fire grilled nyama choma (Kenyan roasted meats), traditional ugali, sukuma wiki, and a decadent Mara honey and ginger cake under a canopy of stars

day_by_day.notes: The hot air balloon flight lasts approximately 1 hour and covers a large portion of the Mara ecosystem. Flights depart around 05:30 — a very early wake-up call is required. The Maasai cultural visit is ethically managed and revenue goes directly to the community. Wear closed shoes and modest clothing for the village visit. This is the most experientially rich day of the trip — camera batteries should be fully charged.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise game drive in the Maasai Mara — a farewell journey through the golden grasslands to soak in the last moments of the migration spectacle. Your guide will take you to favorite spots for one final chance at big cat sightings and river activity. Return to camp for a full breakfast and pack-up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private charter flight from the Maasai Mara airstrip back to Nairobi. Upon arrival, transfer to a premium city hotel or airport lounge for a comfortable transition. Enjoy a final Kenyan lunch at one of Nairobi's top restaurants — Talisman or Carnivore — celebrating the culmination of an extraordinary safari journey.
day_by_day.evening: Private transfer to Jomo Kenyatta International Airport for departure. Enjoy the premium airport lounge with complimentary drinks, light bites, and Wi-Fi while reflecting on an unforgettable 10-day Kenyan adventure. Depart with memories of the Great Migration, northern white rhinos, and the warmth of Maasai culture.

meals.breakfast: Farewell full breakfast at the Maasai Mara camp — a lavish spread of Kenyan favorites including mandazi doughnuts, fresh papaya, eggs any style, crispy bacon, and single-origin Kenyan coffee
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch in Nairobi at Talisman Restaurant — wood-fired artisan pizza, grilled Kenyan lamb chops, roasted vegetable salad, and a final Kenyan chai with homemade cookies
meals.dinner: Premium airport lounge dining or in-flight first-class dining — light mezze, grilled proteins, and a glass of South African Chenin Blanc as a final toast to Kenya

day_by_day.notes: Confirm the charter flight departure time from the Mara the evening before — weather and airstrip conditions can occasionally cause minor delays. Allow at least 3 hours at Nairobi airport for international departures. Purchase Kenyan souvenirs — coffee, Maasai beadwork, and wildlife photography books — at the airport's premium gift shops. Ensure all wildlife-related souvenirs comply with CITES regulations; no ivory, turtle shell, or restricted animal products.
